title: Lechon kawali
intro: Pork belly simmered until tender, then deep-fried until the skin puffs and crackles while the meat stays juicy. It is chopped into chunks and dipped in spiced vinegar or lechon sauce.

items.name: pork belly
items.note: one slab with skin, about 2 inches thick

items.name: salt
items.note: for boiling, plus 1 tsp for rubbing

steps.text: Put the pork in a pot with the salt, peppercorns, bay leaves and garlic. Add water to cover by an inch and bring to a boil, skimming off the scum.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer until a fork slides easily into the meat but the slab still holds its shape.
Lift the pork out and pat it completely dry. Rub the skin with 1 tsp salt and leave it on a rack, skin side up, until the surface feels dry to the touch.
Meanwhile, stir together all the dip ingredients and set aside.
Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pot to 350°F (175°C). Pat the pork dry once more and lower it in carefully, skin side down. Cover loosely with a splatter guard or lid set ajar, as the skin pops.
Fry, turning once or twice, until the skin is deep golden and blistered all over.
Drain on a rack so the bottom stays crisp. Let it rest before cutting.
Chop into bite-size pieces with a heavy knife and serve hot with the dip and steamed rice.

tips: For the crispiest skin, refrigerate the boiled pork uncovered overnight before frying. Any water left on the surface makes the oil spit, so dry it well.

title: Pork barbecue
intro: Thin slices of pork marinated in soy sauce, banana ketchup, soda and calamansi, threaded onto bamboo skewers and grilled with a sweet basting sauce. Sticky, smoky and slightly charred at the edges.

steps.text: Mix all the marinade ingredients in a bowl, add the pork and toss to coat. Cover and refrigerate.
Thread 4 or 5 slices onto each soaked skewer, folding the slices so they bunch up a little.
Pour the leftover marinade into a small pan with the ketchup and oil for basting. Boil it, stirring, until slightly thickened.
Grill the skewers over medium-hot charcoal, turning and basting every couple of minutes, until cooked through and charred in spots.
Serve hot with rice and a dip of vinegar with chopped onion and chili.

tips: Marinate overnight for the best flavor. A grill pan or the broiler works too; line the tray with foil, as the sugary sauce burns onto pans.
